label: GBV Inc.
release_notes: Lineup: Robert Pollard (vocals), Doug Gillard (lead guitar), Bobby Bare Jr. (rhythm guitar), Mark Shue (bass), Kevin March (drums).
12 songs in about 37 minutes; reviewers note a turn back to loud guitar rock after recent prog-leaning records.
Opener Lost in the Sun. You have aired GBV on 92 shows.
Label not in the Zookeeper label table.
Produced by Travis Harrison (Wikipedia). Pollard says it was recorded in a studio with members living in different places (Rolling Stone).
draft_comment: There's something wrong with Robert Pollard. Album number 44, and it rocks like a band half their age. 12 songs, 37 minutes, all killer.

tracks.title: Lost In The Sun
tracks.notes: Opener: feedback blast into big chopped chords (AllMusic). In the Oct. 8 plan. ecoustics compares it to The Who and The Cars, with Mellotron strings and tight harmonies.

tracks.title: Out With A Theory
tracks.notes: About a cover band that starts writing originals and dreams of recording with Mitch Easter (Pollard). Starts with Pollard and heavy electric guitar; the full band enters about halfway (The Fire Note).

tracks.title: We Outlast Them All
tracks.notes: Lead single; Pollard calls it GBV's We Are The Champions. Announced with the album Feb. 25, 2026. Pollard says it was written in one take (Rolling Stone). Called a triumphant anthem (Maximum Volume Music).

tracks.title: A Grand Ceremonial Jester
tracks.notes: Sgt. Pepper-style psych pop carnival in 1:18 (The Fire Note).

tracks.title: Dagon's Plunger
tracks.notes: Builds to a strutting riff over sinister vocals (PopMatters). Some of the album's strongest guitar work (Maximum Volume Music).

tracks.title: Advance Without Dropping
tracks.notes: Aggressive punk energy with melodic turns; GBV at their punkiest (Maximum Volume Music).

tracks.title: Arthur Square
tracks.notes: New Wave-leaning rocker that veers prog (Maximum Volume Music). ecoustics hears a cousin of the 1969 pre-Tommy Who.

tracks.title: Landscaping
tracks.notes: Called a pretty, psychedelic ballad (PopMatters). Altrevue's favorite.

tracks.title: (How Would You Like A) Chariot Ride
tracks.notes: Chord sequence echoes "The Punk and the Godfather" from The Who's Quadrophenia (ecoustics).

tracks.title: When You're My Clown (Nothing Happens)
tracks.notes: Epic closer: heavy chugging riff, then an acoustic-driven coda (ecoustics).
